verdict_reason: The *machine* is now genuinely well designed, and I want to say that plainly: I walked the loop against measured numbers and the hard parts hold up. DOCK_CLEAR_X (5.425) really does clear SECTION_HALF (5.175) so the tire can roll past its own dock without touching it; the tongue tip lands at z=0.830 on a 0.780 landing (0.05 m step, flush enough); the collision deck and the visual ramp agree to the millimetre at all four columns; the 90-degree turn genuinely fits (entering at x=+4.118 heading -X, the far corner sweeps to x=-2.49 in a +-4.118 lane, 1.63 m spare); and the exit is fairer than the code's own comments claim, because at bottom-dead-centre the port's world speed is only omega*(R_outer - R_port) = 0.55 m/s at 30 km/h and it dwells there 0.89 s. That is a real, catchable window, and it means the undocumented best beat in this mod - chasing down a runaway 18-tonne tire and re-boarding it through a nearly-stationary doorway - is actually possible. But as a thing to PLAY it is still blind and still miscounts. The abort beat is dead code (onExit takes an object; the runtime hands it an integer, in a pcall, silently - every other spec in the pack got this right). The only score in the mod is the tire's lifetime odometer, so "NEW BEST" fires on essentially every dismount forever. The exit countdown mathematically always prints "4", then goes silent for 3.4 s, then gives 0.59 s of real warning. The only failure state - tipping - is geometrically reached at 20.18 degrees and detected at 46.05, so the player gets no warning inside the recoverable band and one obituary after it, and is then sealed in a bowl. And there is a hole in the floor at both corners of the doorway. I would stop and stare at the tire. I would not stop and stare at the loop. Also, for honesty: round-1 item 13 was still broken when this review was commissioned - updateRiders iterated `state.subjects`, a table the shared runtime never creates - and was patched at 00:33:49 while I was mid-read. I reviewed the patched version.

At my first read, updateRiders iterated `pairs(state.subjects or {})` and the shared runtime has no `subjects` table anywhere (grepped the whole pack) - the dismount/re-board payoff was still a silent no-op. spec.py and runtime.lua were rewritten to iterate b.tracked at 00:33:49 mid-review. Lane width claim (7.20 -> 8.24 m, 'a car can now turn round inside'): the VALUE landed (2*LINER_HALF = 8.2370) but nothing measures the claim - CAR_TURN_RADIUS is declared and never referenced. See finding 9.

findings.title: behavior.onExit takes an object; the runtime passes an ID, so the abort beat is dead
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:1112 `behavior.onExit` (generated to runtime.lua:852); call sites runtime.lua:1147, 1335, 1345
findings.problem: The shared runtime invokes `pcall(behavior.onExit, state, zone, vehicleId)` at all three call sites, passing a NUMBER. The colossus chunk declares `function(state, zone, vehicle)` and immediately does `local id = vehicle:getId()`, which is an index-a-number error. It is inside the caller's pcall, so it fails silently on every single cabin exit. Every other spec in the pack (bouncy_castle, catapult_seesaw, dino_egg_hatcher, gforce_centrifuge, giant_toaster, monster_flyswatter, pachinko_tower, spin_cycle_washer, spin_launch, vacuum_of_doom, whale_geyser) declares `vehicleId`; colossus_tire is the only one that does not. Consequences the player feels: 'Cabin clear. Tie-downs held.' can never appear; b.aboard and b.aboardCount never decrement, so onEnter's `if b.aboard[id] then return end` also blocks re-entry messaging and countdown re-arm; and there is NO way to abort the release once you have nosed into the cabin trigger - reversing back out over the gangway still cuts the straps 3 s later behind you. The one moment of player choice before the point of no return does not exist.
findings.fix: In spec.py's LUA_BEHAVIOR change the signature to `behavior.onExit = function(state, zone, vehicleId)` and delete the `local id = vehicle:getId()` line, using vehicleId throughout (the body is otherwise correct). Regenerate. Then add a pack-wide gate next to the existing behaviour-node-name gate in tests/test_giant_props_pack.py: for every spec, assert the third parameter name of `behavior.onExit` matches what lua_kit's call sites pass - this is a silent-failure class the pcall will hide again.

findings.title: Score is the tire's lifetime odometer, so NEW BEST fires on every dismount forever
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:1177 `updateRiders` (b.distance / b.revolutions / b.best), against `behavior.update`'s accumulator at spec.py:1259
findings.problem: b.distance and b.revolutions are accumulated unconditionally in behavior.update from the moment the prop registers - they measure the TIRE, not the ride. updateRiders then reports them verbatim on dismount and tests `b.distance > b.best + B.record_min_m`. Because b.distance is monotonically non-decreasing and b.best is only ever set to a past value of it, the record test is true on every dismount after the tire has moved another 25 m, including 25 m it rolled on its own while the player was standing outside watching. So the loop's single piece of scoring is rigged to always congratulate you, and 'CLEAR. 14 revolutions, 612 m' after a 40 m ride is simply the wrong number. A score you cannot lose is not a score, and it kills the only reason to push the ride one revolution further.
findings.fix: In updateRiders' boarding branch (and in behavior.onEnter), snapshot `b.rideDistance0 = b.distance` and `b.rideTurns0 = b.revolutions`. On dismount report `b.distance - b.rideDistance0` and `b.revolutions - b.rideTurns0`, and compare THAT delta against b.best. Add a gate asserting the dismount message's distance term is a difference, not b.distance.

findings.title: Open wedges in the floor at both doorway corners: the gangway is narrower than the cut
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py:2007 (`if sign > 0 and station in PORT_QUADS: continue`) vs examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:561 `TONGUE_HALF_ARC_DEG = 11.5`
findings.problem: The lin_r -> sill_r shoulder band (x 4.1185 to 4.6829, the outboard threshold strip of the cavity floor) is skipped for every station in PORT_QUADS = {46,47,0,1}, i.e. across the full 30 deg port arc, on the stated grounds that 'over the port sector the boarding gangway IS this surface'. It is not: TONGUE_HALF_ARC_DEG is 11.5, so the gangway only covers +-11.5 deg. That leaves two uncovered wedges at theta [-15,-11.5] and [+11.5,+15] - 0.80 m of arc at r=13.15 by 0.565 m axially - with the SIDEWALL_R bands over the same stations also cut by port_open_at. There is nothing under them but daylight. They sit at the two corners of the doorway, the exact strip the car crosses on every board and every bail, and 0.565 m is wide enough to swallow a wheel. This is the same class of defect as round 1's uncut sidewall band, moved 3.5 degrees sideways.
findings.fix: Set `TONGUE_HALF_ARC_DEG = spec.PORT_SPAN_DEG / 2.0` (15.0) so the gangway exactly covers what PORT_QUADS removes - it also widens the boarding surface from a 5.28 m chord to 6.81 m, which is better anyway. Alternatively make the skip condition test the tongue's real arc rather than PORT_QUADS. Then add a gate: for every station in PORT_QUADS, assert a collision triangle exists covering the lin_r..sill_r strip (from the tongue or the shoulder band), so the two surfaces can never drift apart again.

findings.title: The exit countdown always prints the same number, then leaves 0.59 s of real warning
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:1213 `updateExitWindow` (b.exitWarned latch and the `"PORT COMES ROUND IN %.0f"` format)
findings.problem: b.exitWarned latches on the first frame where `remaining < B.exit_lead_seconds`, so remaining is always ~3.999 and `%.0f` always formats to '4'. The string is a constant. At the design spin-up speed (omega = 0.5915 rad/s, 10.62 s per revolution) 4 s out is 135.6 deg away - most of a half-turn, far too early to line up - and then the player hears nothing at all for 3.4 s until 'PORT IS DOWN' fires at the 20 deg threshold, which is 0.59 s before bottom-dead-centre. The manoeuvre being asked for is a 90 deg turn across a moving, banked drum; 0.59 s of actionable notice makes the climax of the loop a coin flip rather than a skill. The comment above the function is right about the diagnosis and the code does not act on it.
findings.fix: Drop the exitWarned latch and emit the remaining time every frame while `remaining < B.exit_lead_seconds` (guihooks.message replaces within a category, so a per-frame refresh is a live countdown, not spam). Format with one decimal below 3 s. Keep 'PORT IS DOWN' as the go signal but raise its threshold from 20 deg to something time-based, e.g. open the window while `math.abs(clock) / rate < 1.2`, so it does not shrink to nothing as the tire speeds up.

findings.title: Tipping is unwarned in the recoverable band and a soft-lock once it happens
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:1247 `updateTipped` (B.tipped_dot = 0.72); gated by tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::test_the_tire_is_not_a_pancake
findings.problem: The tire is geometrically past the point of no return at atan(SECTION_HALF/OUTER_RADIUS) = 20.18 deg of lean, which is |tire.axis.z| = 0.3449. updateTipped does not fire until |axis.z| >= 0.72 = 46.05 deg. So the player gets zero feedback across the entire 0-20 deg band where a lean is still correctable by driving the other way up the wall, and the announcement arrives 26 deg past the point where anything could have been done. Tipping is the ONLY failure state in the loop, and it is invisible until it is an obituary. Worse, the message ('Reset the prop to stand it back up') asks the player to reset a vehicle they are not driving, and by then their car is sealed in a bowl whose only aperture is now a skylight or a manhole. The gate that is supposed to protect this asserts only `0.5 < tipped_dot < 0.95`, a band that never mentions the 20.18 deg geometry it is meant to be consistent with.
findings.fix: In updateTipped, add two earlier beats off the already-computed tire.axis.z: a rising-edge warning at ~0.6 * the geometric tip sine ('SHE IS LEANING - drive up the high side') and a hard one at the geometric value itself ('SHE IS GOING OVER'). Derive both from SECTION_HALF/OUTER_RADIUS rather than typing constants, and tighten the gate to assert the warning threshold is strictly below sin(atan(SECTION_HALF/OUTER_RADIUS)) and tipped_dot strictly above it. Separately, once b.tipped is set, tell the player the actual escape (switch to the Colossus and recover it), since 'reset the prop' is not a control they have while driving.

findings.title: THE ONE CHANGE: the player flies blind - every number they need is computed and discarded
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:1259 `behavior.update` (portClock, tire.axis.z, b.speed, b.distance all live and unused between toasts); examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py:1359 `build_lane_marks`
findings.problem: Everything after 'STRAPS CUT' happens inside a closed torus with no horizon, one aperture that is only open ~8% of each revolution, and 16 IDENTICAL emissive chevrons - build_lane_marks' docstring claims they are 'a landmark' but they are indistinguishable from one another, so they give heading and speed and nothing about WHERE YOU ARE relative to the exit. The runtime already knows all four things the player is missing: portClock(state, tire) is the exact port bearing, tire.axis.z is the lean, b.speed is the speed, b.distance is the ride. All four are discarded except as sporadic 2-second toasts. This is what keeps the loop from being fun: the exit is guesswork rather than a timed skill, the tip-over is invisible, and the best beat in the whole mod - chasing down the runaway tire and re-boarding through a doorway that is nearly world-stationary at the bottom (0.55 m/s, 0.89 s dwell) - is neither signposted nor discoverable. updateRiders will happily say 'Back aboard. Go again.' for a manoeuvre nothing ever tells the player is possible.
findings.fix: Two parts, both cheap. (a) Refresh ONE guihooks.message every frame in UI_CATEGORY while a rider is aboard - same category replaces rather than stacks, so it reads as a persistent HUD line: `PORT v 2.4s | LEAN 11 deg | 34 km/h | 128 m`. Build it from portClock/spin, math.deg(math.asin(math.abs(tire.axis.z))), b.speed*3.6 and the per-ride distance from finding 2. (b) In build_lane_marks, make the run-in to the port legible: give the chevrons at the 2-3 stations before station 0 a distinct colour and put a solid emissive threshold bar at station 0, so the exit is a PLACE you can watch coming instead of the 17th identical arrow. Together these turn the exit from luck into skill and make re-boarding a thing the player can see how to do.

findings.title: Speed, revolution and exit callouts keep firing at a player who already bailed
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:1259 `behavior.update` (the `if b.released then` block) and spec.py:1004 `announceSpeed`
findings.problem: announceSpeed, the revolution announcement, and updateExitWindow are all gated on b.released only, never on anyone being aboard. After a successful dismount the tire keeps rolling - which is the whole point, it is a runaway - and the player, now standing outside, receives 'PORT IS DOWN - go now if you want out' and 'PORT COMES ROUND IN 4' on every revolution, plus band callouts, for a tire that may be 300 m away. Instructions to escape a vehicle you have already escaped read as a bug and undercut the moment you just earned.
findings.fix: Wrap updateExitWindow and the revolution/speed announcements in a `local aboard = next(b.riders) ~= nil` check. Keep a reduced spectator track for the empty case - the revolution/distance line is genuinely good to watch it run away with - but drop the exit prompts entirely when b.riders is empty.

findings.title: Release countdown starts on the trigger edge, so 3..2..1 plays over an emergency stop
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py `behavior.onEnter` (b.countdown = B.release_countdown) with TRIGGERS['cabin'] at spec.py:863
findings.problem: The cabin trigger spans x -3.8 to +3.8, so it fires the instant the nose clears the doorway at x=+4.118 - while the car is still travelling at whatever speed it carried off a 7.1% ramp, still pointing straight across a lane that is only 8.237 m wide before the far sidewall curves up. The 2.4 s 'SUBJECT ABOARD' toast and the 3..2..1 therefore play on top of the player braking hard and hauling the wheel round, and 'STRAPS CUT. The Colossus is loose - DRIVE.' lands while they are typically stopped against the far wall pointing 90 degrees away from any direction that produces torque. The dramatic beat and the mechanical beat are out of phase, and the player's first experience of release is confusion rather than commitment.
findings.fix: Gate the countdown on being aboard AND settled: arm it in behavior.update while the subject is inside the cabin zone and `vehicle:getVelocity():length() < ~2`, rather than on the trigger's rising edge. That puts 'STRAPS CUT' at the moment the player has stopped, turned, and is looking down the barrel - which is the beat the spec's own prose describes.

findings.title: The 'car can turn round inside' claim is gated by a proxy; CAR_TURN_RADIUS is unused
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:251 `CAR_TURN_RADIUS = 5.2`; tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::test_cavity_clears_a_car clearance 3
findings.problem: The headline justification for the size-code change is 'the cavity lane went 7.20 m -> 8.24 m (a car can now turn round inside without shuffling)'. The gate that is supposed to hold that asserts `2 * LINER_HALF > CAR_LENGTH + 2.0`, i.e. 8.2370 > 6.5 - a comparison against the car's LENGTH that has nothing to do with a turning circle and would pass happily at 6.6 m of lane, where the turn is impossible. CAR_TURN_RADIUS, the only constant in the file that describes the manoeuvre, is referenced by nothing: not the generator, not any test. I checked the real number and the geometry does pass - entering at x=+LINER_HALF heading -X, the turn centre sits at x=4.1185 and the outermost corner sweeps sqrt((R+W/2)^2 + (L/2)^2) = 6.604 m, reaching x = -2.486 against a -4.1185 wall, 1.63 m of margin. So the tire is fine; the assertion is not, and this is exactly the 'fixed by changing the thing that measures' pattern to watch for.
findings.fix: Replace clearance 3 with the swept-corner test using CAR_TURN_RADIUS: assert `spec.LINER_HALF - math.hypot(spec.CAR_TURN_RADIUS + spec.CAR_WIDTH/2, spec.CAR_LENGTH/2) > -spec.LINER_HALF + margin`, and state the measured 1.63 m margin in the docstring so a future size-code change that eats it fails loudly.

findings.title: Three round-1 figures survive the 'stale figures corrected' pass
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py:409 (CAVITY_LANE comment), spec.py:1211 (updateExitWindow comment, generated into runtime.lua), tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::test_size_code_produces_the_modelled_tire docstring
findings.problem: spec.py:409 reads `CAVITY_LANE = 2.0 * LINER_HALF  # 8.68 m of flat floor` - the computed value is 8.2370. The Lua comment above updateExitWindow says 'a 90 degree turn in an 8.7 m lane', same stale figure, and it ships inside the mod's runtime.lua. And the gate that enforces the new size code still opens with '8400/80R580 must be the tire that was actually built' - round 1's rejected truck-tire code, sitting in the docstring of the test whose entire job is to prevent exactly that drift. The spec's own module docstring elsewhere correctly says 8.24. Each of these is the number a future reader will trust over the arithmetic, and this is the one item (round 1 #22) whose whole point was to stop that.
findings.fix: Make the two comments render the value instead of restating it (or delete the figure), and rewrite the gate's docstring to name 10350/80R457. Cheap, and it removes the last places where the prose and the measurement disagree.

verdict_reason: Round 1's tread work genuinely landed — I recomputed net-to-gross (0.828 x 0.854 = 70.7%), the shoulder row is now the widest block at 1.482 m, the groove floor is 0.186 m under 0.634 m of depth, the crown arc divides back to a realistic 19.6 mm drop at reference scale, and the port cut is now a true sidewall section with two casing plies and no belts. That is real tire knowledge on the page. But the tire still does not have a shoulder. The outer sidewall lathe clamps at meridian station 0.930 and then runs straight out to r = OUTER_RADIUS at |x| = 4.712, so each shoulder is a smooth, axially-facing annular wall 0.58 m tall that IS the tire's outermost surface — 0.138 m proud of the shoulder-lug crown and 0.572 m outboard of the tread edge — and it terminates in an open, uncapped boundary ring (144 unshared edges per side, measured off the shipped DAE). In profile.jpg, and unmistakably in a hard crop of it, that ring reads as a rim flange with the tread recessed between two of them, which is exactly the truck-tire silhouette round 1 was told to kill; and the buttress wrap it is meant to be continuous with starts 0.572 m outboard of the lug. Underneath that, the "size code is the single source of geometric truth" claim does not survive measurement: the built mesh is 10.650 m across the section (printed 10350) and its bore is 445.6 in (printed R457). And the bead, which round 1 called a bullnose, is still closed with one half-round revolve. I would stop and stare at the wrong thing.
round1_fixes_verified: 1 VISUAL WINDING - landed. Renders are backface-culled and no inside-out surface reads. Note the limit: assert_face_orientation checks which way faces point, not whether a shell closes, so it cannot see the open shoulder ring in finding 1.

2 SILL STATION - landed. spec.MERIDIAN now carries (0.8873, 0.9049) interpolated off the base meridian at exactly (CAVITY_RADIUS-BEAD_RADIUS)/SECTION_HEIGHT, and cross_section() keys sill_l/sill_r off it.

4 SIZE CODE - landed as authored numbers (OD/W 2.722, rim/W 1.122, both asserted in assert_authored_claims) but NOT as built geometry: the mesh measures 10.650 m section width and a 445.6 in bore. See finding 2.

6 TREAD / NET-TO-GROSS - landed, recomputed independently. Land across width 0.828, circumferential land 0.854, product 70.7%. Shoulder row is now the widest block (1.482 m vs 1.283 and 0.662). Root growth 0.085/side leaves a 0.186 m groove floor. All match the spec's claims.

7 LETTERING - landed. build_lettering computes lowest = BEAD_RADIUS + margin, highest = PROTECTOR_RADII[0] - margin, raises SystemExit on negative slack, and centres the stack. No band interpenetration in hero.jpg or sidewall_print.jpg; relief 0.040 with a bevel reads as moulded, not as a sticker.

8/9 SIDEWALL MOULD RIPPLE - landed. tire_sidewall now uses _stripes(size, ripples, axis=0), i.e. varying along v = meridian arc length, so the iso-lines are concentric circles. Visible as concentric fine lines in shoulder.jpg.

10 PORT LAMINATE SECTION - landed, and it is the best tire-engineering asset in the mod. tire_laminate(section='sidewall') is liner / tie gum / two casing plies / cushion gum / sidewall compound, with brass cord rows drawn only in the two plies and no belt package. Correct for a radial sidewall cut.
16 BUTTRESS FEATHER - landed. add_buttress ends on BUTTRESS_FEATHER = 0.028 rather than zero, so outer_row and inner_row are no longer coincident.

3 CROWN ARC - landed and realistic. TREAD_ARC_RADIUS 62 m gives 0.138 m of crown drop across the 4.140 m tread half, which divides back to 19.6 mm at the 59/80R63 reference. That is a real earthmover crown, not one flattened to fake a footprint.

BEAD (three meridian stations) - NOT landed as a bead. The three stations sit above the bead base; the closure across the base is still a single half-round revolve with no seat, no toe and no heel. See finding 3.

findings.title: The tire has no shoulder: a smooth open flange ring is its outermost surface
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py::build_carcass, the shell()/lathe_rows() pair driven by meridian_fractions() running to fraction 1.0; root cause is spec.py::_MERIDIAN_BASE ending at (0.930, 0.866)
findings.problem: sidewall_mid() clamps to the last meridian station for any fraction above 0.930, so every lathe row from fraction 0.930 (r = 13.504) to 1.000 (r = 14.084) sits at the same half width. The outer sidewall therefore becomes a 0.58 m tall, axially-facing annular wall at |x| = 4.712 reaching r = 14.084 - the same radius as the crown centre, and 0.138 m PROUD of the shoulder-lug crown at 13.946. It is smooth, unbroken, and it is the tire's outermost surface, so the Colossus stands on two rubber flanges with the whole shoulder row 138 mm clear of the ground. It is also open: parsing the shipped ericrolph_colossus_tire.dae, the edge ring at |x| = 4.7 / r = 14.1 is used by exactly one triangle 144 times per side (576 boundary-vertex hits), and the tread base's outboard edge at |x| = 4.14 / r = 13.31 is a separate open ring - nothing spans the 0.572 m between them. What a tire person sees: the tread is not the outside of the tire; profile.jpg has a bright smooth rib flanking the blocks on both sides (a hard crop makes it unmistakable), which is exactly the truck-tire read round 1 was told to kill; and the buttress wrap, sold as the shoulder lug continuing down the sidewall, begins 0.572 m outboard of the lug's outer face at 4.140, so it is a detached raised patch on a flange, not a wrap. The collision cage already has the right shape - build_cage's crown-to-shoulder quad ties crn_r (x 4.140, r 13.946) straight to shl_r (x 4.482, r 13.504) - so the physics tire and the visible tire disagree about where the shoulder is.
findings.fix: Stop the outer and inner lathes at the last real meridian station (fraction 0.930) instead of 1.0, and loft an explicit shoulder surface from that row to the tread base's outboard rings at (TREAD_HALF, crown_r(TREAD_HALF)) and (TREAD_HALF, base_r(TREAD_HALF)) - the same two rings the cage already joins. Add two or three meridian stations past 0.930 that turn the profile inboard (e.g. (0.955, 0.845), (0.975, 0.815)) so the outer profile lands tangentially on the tread edge instead of going vertical, and re-anchor add_buttress's top row to crown_r(TREAD_HALF) at |x| = TREAD_HALF so the wrap starts on the lug it continues. Then add a gate that walks the built visual mesh, collects edges used by exactly one triangle, and fails the build if any lies outside the known groove-floor/lug-root set - assert_face_orientation cannot catch this class of defect.

findings.title: Mesh does not match the size code: 10650 mm section width, 445.6 in bore
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py::_MERIDIAN_BASE station (0.600, 1.000) with SIDEWALL_THICKNESS, and create_colossus_tire.py::build_carcass's bead-toe cap line `radius -= math.sin(angle) * spec.SIDEWALL_THICKNESS[0] * 0.22`
findings.problem: The spec's headline claim, made three times, is that the size code is the generator's input so 'the moulded lettering and the mesh can never disagree'. They disagree. MERIDIAN is documented as the STRUCTURAL MID-SHELL, but its half-width fractions are taken against SECTION_HALF, so station (0.600, 1.000) puts the mid-shell at 5.175 and shell() then adds thickness/2 - the outer rubber surface peaks at 5.325, a measured section width of 10.650 m against a printed 10350. Measured off the shipped DAE on the port-free sidewall, maximum half width is 5.386 m (5.325 plus the 0.040 letter relief). At the other end the bead cap pulls the profile 0.145 m below BEAD_RADIUS, so the global minimum radius in the mesh is 5.6587 m - a bore of 445.6 inches against a printed R457. A 457 in rim physically will not enter this tire, and the aspect ratio the mesh realises is 79.1, not 80. Every derived number in spec.py (SCALE, TREAD_DEPTH, MAX_LOAD_KG, OD_TO_WIDTH, RIM_TO_WIDTH) comes from the authored code, and assert_authored_claims only checks those authored numbers against each other - nothing ever measures the built mesh.
findings.fix: Either author _MERIDIAN_BASE as the OUTER surface and derive the mid-shell as half - thickness/2 inside sidewall_mid(), or divide the half-width fractions so that max(half + thick/2) lands exactly on SECTION_HALF. Make the bead-toe cap tangent at r = BEAD_RADIUS instead of pulling below it (finding 3 fixes both at once). Then extend assert_authored_claims to measure the built mesh: max |x| over the carcass objects must equal SECTION_HALF to within a few millimetres and min radius must equal BEAD_RADIUS, failing the build otherwise. That is the assert that would make the size-code claim true.

findings.title: The bead is still a bullnose; the three new stations never reach the bead base
findings.where: create_colossus_tire.py::build_carcass, the 'Bead toe: close the shell across its thickness with a rounded toe' block; spec.py::_MERIDIAN_BASE stations (0.000, 0.732) and (0.055, 0.760)
findings.problem: spec.py says a single station closed with a half-round cap is 'a rubber bullnose, not a bead' and claims the fix is three stations giving 'the seat taper a real bead sits on'. The three stations were added, but they all sit ABOVE the bead base - the closure ACROSS the base is unchanged: one semicircular revolve of radius 0.33 m swept between the outer face at |x| = 4.118 and the inner face at 3.458, both at r = BEAD_RADIUS, with a sinusoidal radial pull of 0.145 m. There is no flat or conical bead seat anywhere on the tire, no toe corner, no heel radius, and no chafer break. hero.jpg's bead aperture is 8.28 m off the ground and unavoidable in every wide shot because the tire ships with no rim, and it reads as a rounded rubber lip. Separately, the taper the two new stations do describe is wrong by construction: toe to heel is 0.4554 m radially for 0.1449 m axially, which is 72.4 degrees off the axial direction - an OTR rim bead seat is 5 degrees, so this profile climbs 3.1x its axial run where a real one climbs 0.09x.
findings.fix: Replace the half-round cap with an authored bead-base profile in the (half width, radius) plane: a toe corner at (0.732*SECTION_HALF, BEAD_RADIUS) with a small radius, a straight seat run outboard at 5 degrees rising to the heel, a heel radius, then hand off to the existing station at fraction 0.055. Hold the whole seat run at radius >= BEAD_RADIUS so the bore matches R457. Give the seat and heel their own tire_bead material band so the burnished rim-bearing area reads, and drive the flange-rise station's half width off RIM_TO_WIDTH rather than the hand-typed 0.760.

findings.title: Row phasing eats the lateral groove: 0.151-0.569 m where 0.360 is authored
findings.where: create_colossus_tire.py::build_tread, the `a0 = start + span * phase + groove_angle * 0.5` / `a1 = end + span * phase - groove_angle * 0.5` pair, plus the `add_tie_bar(detail, a1, a1 + groove_angle, ...)` call
findings.problem: The row phase is applied as a fraction of each pitch's OWN span, so at a pitch-length change the two neighbouring lugs shift by different amounts and the lateral groove between them absorbs the whole difference. Computed straight off spec.PITCH_SEQUENCE and PITCH_RATIOS at GROOVE_RADIUS: row 0 (phase 0.0) holds 0.360 m exactly, but row 1 (phase 0.5) swings 0.151 to 0.569 m - a 3.8:1 spread on a nominal 0.360 m groove - and row 2 (phase 0.22) swings 0.268 to 0.452 m. That is backwards from how designed pitch variation works: the groove is the constant and the LAND varies. It shows in profile.jpg as ragged, unevenly spaced lateral grooves in the intermediate rows, and it undercuts the noise argument in the spec, because a groove width that modulates with the pitch sequence re-couples the excitation to the pitch period. The tie bar makes it worse: add_tie_bar is always groove_angle wide, so on the 0.151 m grooves it buries 0.209 m of itself inside the neighbouring lug, and on the 0.569 m grooves it leaves 0.209 m of unbarred groove floor.
findings.fix: Phase the rows on the GLOBAL pitch grid, not on each row's local span: build the pitch boundary list once, then for a phased row offset every boundary by phase * (mean pitch), a constant arc, so the groove keeps its authored width everywhere and only the lug length varies. Derive the tie bar's angular width from the actual gap (next pitch's a0 minus this pitch's a1) instead of assuming groove_angle. Add a gate alongside the net-to-gross assert that measures min/max lateral groove width per row and fails outside about +/-10% of spec.LATERAL_GROOVE.

findings.title: TKPH 850 is the reference tire's number, next to a MAX LOAD that was scaled
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py, `TKPH = 850` and the PALETTE entry for {MOD_ID}_sidewall_print, line f"TKPH {TKPH}   TUBELESS"
findings.problem: Round 1's lesson was that MAX LOAD must be derived, not copied, and MAX_LOAD_KG is now correctly REFERENCE_MAX_LOAD * SCALE**2 = 4,963,968 kg. TKPH did not get the same treatment and is still the 59/80R63's own figure. TKPH is mean tire load in tonnes times mean speed in km/h; at half the printed max load that is 2,482 t, so TKPH 850 says this tire may be worked at 0.34 km/h. Heat generation goes as load x speed and dissipation goes as surface area, so on the same scaling argument the spec already uses for load it should read roughly 850 * SCALE**2 ~ 42,000. As shipped it is the one number on the sidewall that came from nowhere, printed one line below the number that was fixed for exactly that reason.
findings.fix: Derive it: TKPH = 850 * SCALE**2, rounded, placed in the derived-constants block next to MAX_LOAD_KG with the same one-line justification. While in that string, drop the duplicated tubeless marking - SERVICE_CODE already prints 'TL' and the load line prints 'TUBELESS', and no real sidewall carries both.

findings.title: A DOT TIN on an E-4 rock tire; an earthmover carries NHS instead
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py, BUILD_CODE = "DOT XR 9K CLS8 3426" and SERVICE_CODE = "E-4  ***  TL  RADIAL"
findings.problem: The TIN format itself is correct (2-char plant, 2-char size, 4 optional, 4-digit date, week 34 of 2026) and the comment shows the author knows the rule - but the rule applies to tires intended for public roads. An E-4 rock-service earthmover is not one; a 59/80R63 carries 'NHS' (Not for Highway Service) and the manufacturer's own serial, not a DOT TIN. Anyone who has stood next to one of these looks for NHS on the flank before anything else. The sidewall also omits two markings that ARE standard on an OTR flank and would cost nothing: the rim designation the tire is moulded for, and REGROOVABLE, which an E-4 rock tire almost always is.
findings.fix: Replace BUILD_CODE's DOT prefix with a serial in the OTR idiom and add NHS to SERVICE_CODE - e.g. SERVICE_CODE = "E-4  ***  TL  RADIAL  NHS", BUILD_CODE = "SER XR9K CLS8 3426". Add one more line to the sidewall_print lines tuple: f"RIM {RIM_DIAMETER_IN} x {rim_width:.0f}   REGROOVABLE", with rim_width derived from MERIDIAN[0][1] * SECTION_WIDTH so it cannot drift from the bead.

findings.title: Stone ejectors are 220 mm wide in a 186 mm groove floor
findings.where: create_colossus_tire.py::add_ejector, called from build_tread's TREAD_GROOVES loop; spec.py STONE_EJECTOR_R = 0.110 against the floor width implied by TREAD_GROOVES and LUG_ROOT_FILLET + LUG_DRAFT
findings.problem: The circumferential groove is 0.356 m at the top and, after the lug root grows 0.085 per side, 0.186 m at the floor - the number assert_authored_claims checks. add_ejector builds a dome of radius 0.110, so it spans 0.220 m centred on the groove and its base pushes 0.017 m into the root fillet on each side. It is a self-intersection rather than a hole, so nothing catches it, but the ejector reads as merged into both groove walls instead of standing in the floor, and at 0.105 m tall in a 0.634 m groove it is doing very little of the job it is named for. The underlying cause is that the groove floor is 3.4:1 deep-to-wide, narrow even for rock service.
findings.fix: Derive the ejector radius from the floor instead of typing it: radius = 0.40 * ((hi - lo) * TREAD_HALF - 2 * (LUG_ROOT_FILLET + LUG_DRAFT)), which gives 0.074 m here and tracks the row table. If you would rather keep 0.110, widen TREAD_GROOVES to about 0.105 of TREAD_HALF (0.435 m top, 0.265 m floor) - net-to-gross drops to roughly 0.68, still inside NET_TO_GROSS_BAND, and the groove aspect becomes much more like a real E-4. Add the fit check to assert_authored_claims beside the existing groove-floor assert.

findings.title: Port cut-edge ply steps do not line up with the laminate texture's ply boundaries
findings.where: create_colossus_tire.py::build_port, the `steps = spec.PORT_CUT_STEPS` / `relief = (0.000, -0.012, 0.006, 0.004, -0.010, 0.002, 0.000)` block, against proplib/texture_kit.py::tire_laminate's sidewall band table
findings.problem: The cut edge is the most expert surface on the prop and the texture behind it is excellent, but the geometry and the texture disagree about where the plies are. The 7 rows are placed at uniform t = step/6, so the geometric steps land at v = 0.167, 0.333, 0.500, 0.667, 0.833, while tire_laminate's sidewall interfaces are at v = 0.100, 0.160, 0.380, 0.560, 0.640. Under raking light the relief steps sit in the middle of painted layers instead of on their edges. Separately, the relief is applied as a radius offset (`radius + relief[step] * 0.5`), which is normal to the cut face only along the sill and the header; down the two vertical edges of the doorway the cut normal is circumferential, so the offset slides along the face and produces no relief at all on half the opening - including the edge a car's headlights rake as it turns in.
findings.fix: Drive the rows off the texture's own band table rather than a uniform ladder: export the sidewall layer boundaries from tire_laminate (or mirror them as a tuple in spec.py) and place one row at each interface, so the geometry steps and the painted interfaces are the same list. Apply the relief along the perimeter's outward direction, the (out_t, out_r) that port_perimeter() already returns, instead of along radius, so all four edges of the opening get the step.

verdict_reason: The round-1 winding fix genuinely landed — my own generalized-winding-number test on 988 faces across all 12 materials found zero systematic inversions, and tessellation/shading are clean (3.3 mm sagitta, 0.26-0.45 deg median dihedral, 0.0% tangent seams on every major rubber surface). But I am not wowed, for two reasons that are both measurable on the shipped DAE rather than inferred. First, the budget is spent backwards from the brief: sidewall lettering takes 80,776 tris (45.0% of the budget) to cover 105 m2 (1.9% of the surface), while the cavity liner — the surface the entire mod exists for, the one the player drives on — gets 14,108 tris (7.9%) over 1,892 m2 (33%), i.e. one 37 cm triangle per patch of floor. floor.jpg, cabin.jpg, port_close.jpg and gangway.jpg all show the consequence: acres of bare grey shell with painted chevrons and no moulded geometry whatsoever. That is the opposite of "spare no polygon" on the one surface the user described the mod by. Second, roughly half of that 45% is not even visible: a `max(local.z, 0.0)` clamp in build_lettering collapses the entire back half of every letter onto one plane (measured: exactly 50.0% of print vertices on a single standoff; 13,036 tris with exactly zero UV area). So ~40,000 triangles — 22% of the whole mod — are an invisible coplanar back cap. And the gate that was supposed to catch all of this measures the collision mesh, not the exported mesh, so 34 zero-area triangles, 36 coincident pairs, 74 non-manifold edges and 8,226 winding-inconsistent edges shipped unnoticed. The tread and shoulder are good work; the mod is competent, not stop-and-stare.
round1_fixes_verified: #1 VISUAL WINDING - LANDED. Independent generalized-winding-number test (offset centroids +/- along the face normal, solid-angle sum over all 179,400 tris) on 988 sampled faces across all 12 materials: 0 systematic inversions, only 2 local ones in `steel`. The old inside-out sidewall/cavity-floor bug is genuinely gone. verify_render.py:80 does set use_backface_culling=True on every material.

#1 assert_face_orientation COVERAGE - DOES NOT HOLD. It matches on object-name fragment and `continue`s when no rule matches. build_lettering names its objects `{MOD_ID}_letter_{index}`, which matches none of the 11 fragments in ORIENTATION_RULES, so the 80,776-triangle lettering (45.0% of the budget) is unchecked. It also tolerates 2% inverted faces per object and skips faces with |dot|<0.55.

#16/19/20/22 'Degenerate triangles: 0' - DOES NOT HOLD for the visual mesh. The gate (test_no_degenerate_or_duplicated_collision_triangles) reads handoff['triangles'], the jbeam COLLISION mesh. The shipped DAE has 34 exactly-zero-area triangles (10 `steel`, 24 `steel_worn`) plus 36 exactly-coincident duplicate pairs and 74 non-manifold edges. The generator's `dropped` counter only counts faces its own Mesh.face refused, not faces produced by bpy.ops.object.convert on the text curves.
#21 GATES - the 13 colossus gates plus the pack gates never parse the exported .dae. test_handoff_hashes_match_daes only hashes it. There is no geometry gate on the visual mesh at all.

#7 LETTERING band overlap - LANDED. Bands are stacked and centred by construction in build_lettering with a fit assert; I found no band interpenetration. But the shipped relief is (extrude + bevel_depth) * 2 = 62.4 mm, not the 40 mm LETTER_RELIEF the work order quotes.

UV metric density / closure - MOSTLY GOOD. Density is coherent within surface class (rubber 0.35-0.70 UV/m, hardware 1.0-2.2). Mixed UV handedness looked alarming (tread +24,856/-20,160) but I checked locality: adjacent-triangle handedness flips are 0.0% on liner, sidewall, sidewall_print and bead, so it is benign island mirroring, not tangent seams. Only tread (6.2%) and the small strap/steel_worn parts flip across shared edges.

SMOOTH/FLAT SHADING - GOOD, no finding. 145 circumferential stations give a 3.3 mm chord sagitta at R=14.08; median dihedral is 0.26 deg (liner), 0.45 deg (sidewall), 0.47 deg (tread). The faceting I thought I saw in cabin.jpg is lighting, not geometry.

WATERTIGHTNESS - the carcass has 7,364 boundary edges, but I could not show they are visible: GWN at boundary midpoints clusters near 0.5 because the mesh is globally open, so the test cannot discriminate buried lug bottoms from exposed ones. Not reported as a finding.

findings.title: No gate reads the exported .dae, so 45% of the budget ships unchecked
findings.where: tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::test_no_degenerate_or_duplicated_collision_triangles and ::test_collision_triangles_face_the_right_way; tests/test_giant_props_pack.py::test_handoff_hashes_match_daes; examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py::ORIENTATION_RULES / assert_face_orientation / main (the `dropped` counter, line ~2420)
findings.problem: Both round-1 geometry gates read handoff['triangles'] — the jbeam COLLISION mesh — and the pack gate only hashes the DAE. Nothing parses the shipped visual mesh. assert_face_orientation is the only visual check and it matches on object-name fragment, `continue`-ing when no rule matches; build_lettering names its objects `{MOD_ID}_letter_{index}`, matching none of the 11 fragments, so the 80,776-triangle lettering is checked by nothing. It also allows 2% inverted faces per object and skips faces with |dot|<0.55. The `dropped` counter behind 'degenerate: 0' only counts faces the generator's own Mesh.face refused — it cannot see faces produced by bpy.ops.object.convert on the text curves or by the port/gangway builders. Measured on ericrolph_colossus_tire.dae: 34 exactly-zero-area triangles (10 `steel`, 24 `steel_worn`), 36 exactly-coincident duplicate pairs, 74 non-manifold edges, 8,226 winding-inconsistent shared edges, and a total of 183,328 triangles against the claimed 179,872. This is the exact trap the brief warned about: the fix changed the thing that measures, and it measures a different mesh.
findings.fix: Add a gate in tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py that parses mod/vehicles/ericrolph_colossus_tire/ericrolph_colossus_tire.dae directly (ElementTree over library_geometries; the <triangles> streams give VERTEX/NORMAL/TEXCOORD indices) and asserts, on the shipped triangles: zero faces with area < 1e-9; zero duplicate welded vertex triples; zero non-manifold edges; and zero winding-inconsistent manifold edges (an undirected edge whose two uses run the same direction). Separately, in assert_face_orientation, replace the silent `continue` with a hard failure listing any object that matched no rule, so a new object class can never again enter the export unchecked.

findings.title: max(local.z, 0.0) collapses half of every letter: ~40k invisible tris
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py::build_lettering, the vertex bend loop: `stand = half + thick * 0.5 + sidewall_relief(radius) + max(local.z, 0.0) * 2.0`
findings.problem: Blender's curve.extrude is symmetric about local z=0, so every vertex with local.z <= 0 — the entire back cap of each glyph plus its lower bevel ring — is clamped to the same standoff and lands on one plane. Measured in the shipped DAE: in clean radius bands (R 7-8, 9-10, 11-12) exactly 50.0% of sidewall_print vertices sit at the single minimum standoff. 13,036 of the 80,776 print triangles have exactly zero UV area and are flat-shaded — those are the collapsed back caps, with an undefined tangent basis. The cost is roughly 40,000 triangles (22% of the whole mod) on a back face coplanar with its own base ring: invisible, z-fighting with the base where it overlaps, and the source of 916 slivers, 11,064 sub-cm2 triangles and 6,774 of the 8,226 winding-inconsistent edges (recalc_face_normals cannot orient a shell that is locally flat). As a side effect the shipped relief is (extrude + bevel_depth) * 2 = 62.4 mm, not the 40 mm LETTER_RELIEF the work order quotes.
findings.fix: Stop clamping and start shifting. Set `back = spec.LETTER_RELIEF * 0.5 + spec.LETTER_RELIEF * spec.LETTER_BEVEL` and use `stand = half + thick * 0.5 + sidewall_relief(radius) + (local.z + back)`, dropping the `* 2.0` so the moulded relief equals LETTER_RELIEF as documented. Then delete the now-flush back cap before the bend (bmesh, select faces whose normal points inboard at local z == -back) so the glyph is a capped front shell rather than a closed prism. That returns ~40k triangles and removes the zero-UV-area faces, the slivers and the winding inconsistency in one move.

findings.title: Budget is inverted: cavity floor gets 7.9%, sidewall type gets 45%
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py::build_carcass (liner meridian/station counts) vs ::build_lettering; visible in authoring/verify/floor.jpg, cabin.jpg, port_close.jpg, gangway.jpg
findings.problem: Per-material counts measured on the shipped DAE: sidewall_print 80,776 tris (45.0% of budget) over 105.4 m2 (1.9% of surface); tread 45,016 (25.1%) over 2,454 m2; sidewall 32,616 (18.2%) over 1,085 m2; liner 14,108 (7.9%) over 1,892 m2 (33%). The liner is 0.134 m2 per triangle — a 37 cm triangle — while the lettering is 1.3 cm2 per triangle, a 1000x density difference in favour of the surface nobody drives on. The renders confirm it: floor.jpg, cabin.jpg, port_close.jpg and gangway.jpg show the cavity as a bare grey shell with painted chevrons and zero moulded geometry — no liner splice ridge, no bead-ledge step, no ply overlap, no vent spew, no repair patch, nothing. The user's brief is 'a vehicle can drive around INSIDE it'; the interior is the hero surface and it is the least-resolved thing in the mod.
findings.fix: Spend the ~40k triangles freed by the build_lettering fix on the liner instead of returning them to the type. Concretely, in build_carcass add moulded interior features on the liner's existing station grid: a continuous longitudinal splice ridge (a few cm proud, one per liner half), a stepped bead-ledge shoulder where the liner meets the sidewall, and periodic ply-overlap bands. Raise the liner's meridian sample count so the driving lane is nearer 0.02 m2/triangle rather than 0.134, and cut BRAND_COPIES from 3 to 2 to pay for it.

findings.title: 36 exactly-coincident duplicate triangles z-fight on the port collar
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py::build_port — the `steel` geometry around x -5.41, y 2.13..2.28, z 6.25..6.38
findings.problem: 36 pairs of triangles in the `steel` material share the identical welded vertex triple and the identical material — not double-sided sheets (I checked: zero cross-material duplicate groups), just the same face emitted twice. Two exactly coplanar, exactly coincident faces have no depth ordering, so the port collar will shimmer in engine as the camera moves. The same 20 cm of geometry also carries the 10 exactly-zero-area triangles (e.g. tri 100292, verts at [-5.5329, 2.178, 0.9693], [-5.735, 2.1796, 0.9598], [-5.735, 2.1796, 0.9598] — two identical corners) and 58 of the 74 non-manifold edges. It reads as one loop in build_port emitting its ring twice and closing on a duplicated station.
findings.fix: In build_port, dedupe the collar ring emission — key each face on its sorted rounded vertex triple and skip a repeat — and drop the wrap-around station that duplicates the seam (the ring closes on itself, so the last station must reuse index 0 rather than emit a coincident copy). Then let the new DAE gate from finding 1 assert zero duplicate triples so this cannot come back.

findings.title: Lane chevrons are flat 3.46 m chords on a 13.15 m cylinder: 114 mm error
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py::build_lane_marks; visible in authoring/verify/floor.jpg and port_close.jpg
findings.problem: All 64 lane_mark triangles sit at a single constant radius of 13.138 m with edge lengths up to 3.46 m (median 2.78 m), while the liner they lie on is tessellated at 0.57 m stations. A 3.46 m flat chord on R=13.15 misses the cylinder by 114 mm at mid-span, and the chevron vertices are already 12 mm inside the liner's nominal 13.15 m radius — so each arm is buried in rubber in the middle and standing proud at the ends. In floor.jpg and port_close.jpg the chevron arms are visibly dead-straight lines cutting across a curved floor, with hard aliased edges, and the lower-left chevron in port_close.jpg reads as clipping into the wall. They are also 96 open boundary edges of coplanar decal sheet with no depth bias, which in engine is a z-fight rather than a decal.
findings.fix: Build the chevrons on the liner's own station grid: subdivide each arm so no edge exceeds the liner station pitch (0.57 m), and place each vertex by evaluating the same liner surface function the floor uses, plus a constant 15-20 mm outward standoff instead of the current 12 mm inward offset. That makes them conform, removes the buried mid-spans and puts them safely in front of the floor for depth sorting.

findings.title: Tread normal-map tangents flip across 3,960 shared edges
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py::build_tread — the UV assignment on the lug walls and base band
findings.problem: Signed UV area flips handedness across 3,960 of 64,380 shared tread edges (6.2%), 720 of them between two smooth-shaded triangles. Everything else in the mod is clean — liner, sidewall, sidewall_print and bead are all 0.0% — so this is a local tread UV problem, not the benign left/right island mirroring the raw +24,856/-20,160 split first suggested. Where handedness flips between smooth neighbours, the averaged per-vertex tangent collapses toward zero and the rubber normal map lights inconsistently along that line, reading as a faint crease down some lug flanks. Blender's renders will not show it because EEVEE resolves tangents per-face.
findings.fix: In build_tread, make the UV winding follow the geometric winding for every lug-wall and base-band quad — emit UV corners in the same rotational order as the position corners rather than from a fixed template — so the signed UV area sign is uniform within each lug shell. Add sign-of-UV-area consistency across shared edges to the DAE gate from finding 1.

findings.title: Dock/gangway: 24 zero-area tris, 488 slivers, a 24-triangle 255 m2 deck
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py::build_dock — the `steel_worn` gangway grating and the `deck` surface
findings.problem: The ericrolph_colossus_tire_visual mesh (3,928 tris) carries 24 exactly-zero-area triangles in `steel_worn` (e.g. tri 270, verts at [-18.42, 4.85, 0.03] and [-18.42, 4.85, 0.03] — a repeated corner), 488 slivers below 0.02 quality, 12 non-manifold and 12 winding-inconsistent edges, and 1,320 of its 3,928 triangles are under 1 cm2. Meanwhile the `deck` is 24 triangles spanning 255 m2 at 0.625 UV/m — the coarsest-textured surface in the mod, and it fills the foreground of dock.jpg and the lower third of cabin.jpg. The whole mesh is 100% flat-shaded, which is right for plate steel but leaves the concrete pad reading as folded card.
findings.fix: In build_dock, route the gangway grating through the same area-rejecting face emitter the carcass uses so the repeated-corner quads never reach the mesh, and merge the sliver band at the grating perimeter. Subdivide the deck to roughly 1 m quads and raise its UV density to match the gangway's 1.43 UV/m so the two do not read as different resolutions side by side.

verdict_reason: The sRGB fix is real and clean — I decoded all 11 shipped colour maps back to linear and 10 of 11 land within 6% of the authored palette albedo (tread 0.0431 vs 0.043, liner 0.0879 vs 0.088, steel 0.4268 vs 0.440); the transfer function is the correct piecewise OETF, applied to colour only, opted in on every entry. The concentric-ripple fix landed (25 mm period carries 67-81% of sidewall power on the meridian axis, ~1% circumferentially). The lattice (19 mm), the diamond plate (50 mm, and the only material in the mod whose UV is exactly metric at ratio 1.00), the laminate-is-a-sidewall-section, and the partition-of-unity bands all landed as claimed. But none of that is what the player sees. I mipped every roughness map down the ladder: outside the tread, all of them collapse by mip 3-4 — the sidewall goes from std 0.204 to 0.044 by 40 mm, the liner from 0.054 to 0.009. So at any framing where a 28 m object actually fits on screen, every surface on this tire is a uniform roughness with a uniform albedo, and hero.jpg / profile.jpg / cabin.jpg show exactly that: flat grey mass, featureless grey drum. The one map that does survive to distance, the tread roughness, survives as a single 0.7 m polish blotch carrying 77% of its power at the tile fundamental — a repeating artefact, not a feature. On top of that the circumferential UV never closes on the tread or the cavity floor (I pulled 0.909 m and 1.027 m mismatches straight out of the shipped DAE), 45% of the visual triangle budget carries a legend texture on a bounding-box UV, four shipped normal maps are provably blank, and the night-lighting feature erases its own artwork. findings.title: Spin-up solve divides by axle inertia; the tire rolls, so it needs I_cm + M*R^2
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py TIRE_MASS (L435) and the mass-solve docstring (L75-110); tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::test_carcass_inertia_supports_the_playability_solve (L344, `alpha = torque / inertia`)
findings.problem: The solve computes alpha = T / I where I is the moment of inertia about the AXLE (2.8685e6 kg m^2, which I reproduced from the node positions). But nothing holds this axle: the tire rolls freely on the ground, so the same 18000 kg must also be accelerated LINEARLY. Rigorous moment balance about the axle plus linear momentum gives I_eff = I_cm + M*R^2 + m*R*(R - r*cos(phi)) = 2.869e6 + 3.571e6 + 0.069e6 = 6.508e6 kg m^2. The missing M*R^2 term is LARGER than I_cm itself. With T = 112.4 kNm (which is correct), alpha = 0.01727 rad/s^2 and the tire takes 34.3 s to reach 30 km/h, not 15.1 s -- outside spec.SPINUP_SECONDS_BAND (9-24 s), and that is with zero rolling loss. Energy check confirms it: the spec budgets the 502 kJ of spin energy and omits the 625 kJ of translational energy of the same body. The gate passes because it reproduces the same wrong denominator. This is the same class of error as the round-1 double-count, one line further down: the numerator was fixed and the denominator was not.
findings.fix: In spec.py replace the admissible-inertia step with I_eff = I_cm + M*R^2 + m*R*(R - CAVITY_RADIUS*cos(phi_max)) and re-derive TIRE_MASS. Holding the stated 15 s target gives roughly 7800 kg (I_cm + M*R^2 = M*(k^2 + R^2) = M*357.7). Either ship ~7800 kg or restate the target. In test_carcass_inertia_supports_the_playability_solve compute the same I_eff from the measured positions rather than `inertia` alone, so the gate can never again certify a fixed-axle answer for a rolling body.

Stations 47/00/01 on the r side are strictly interior to the opening, so low_r, max_r and upp_r each leave three collidable nodes floating in the doorway. Measured from the handoff, with the sill (cavity floor) at z=0.9335: upp_r_j00 sits at y=0.000, z=1.408 -- 0.474 m above the floor, exactly on the centreline the car drives through; upp_r_j47/j01 at y=+/-1.655, 0.583 m up; max_r_j47/00/01 at 2.38-2.47 m up, i.e. roof height for anything taller than a hatchback. BeamNG node-vs-triangle collision is cross-vehicle, so these are invisible hard points that will kick the car as it boards. The port cut is otherwise correct (r-side only, 4 quads per band, SILL station on a node ring), which is what makes this so easy to miss.
findings.fix: In build_cage, after the skin loop, walk the r-side sidewall rings and set collision=False on every node whose station is strictly interior to PORT_QUADS (47, 0, 1 for low_r/max_r/upp_r) -- keep the nodes and their port_frame beams so the doorway keeps its structural ring, just take them out of the collision set. Add a gate in tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py that sweeps a CAR_WIDTH x CAR_HEIGHT box through the port at the sill and asserts it contains no node with collision:true.

findings.title: Gangway cannot rest on the dock: selfCollision false on a same-vehicle contact
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py build_cage tongue block (L2128-2172); every node row in mod/vehicles/ericrolph_colossus_tire/ericrolph_colossus_tire.jbeam carries "selfCollision": false
findings.problem: spec.py's premise is that the tongue rests on the dock landing plate "the way a ship's gangway rests on a quay". It cannot: the tongue and the dock are nodes of the SAME jbeam vehicle, and BeamNG only tests a node against its own vehicle's triangles when selfCollision is set. It is false on all 1090 nodes. Settling the shipped cage confirms it -- tongue_r2_c0..c5 drop 0.84-1.10 m straight through the landing plate (fixed at z=0.780) and come to rest on the terrain at z~0.000. With a 1600 kg car on the deck the tip settles to z=0.088-0.189, about 0.6-0.7 m BELOW the plate it is supposed to bridge to, and the root row sags to 0.763-0.847. So the boarding route is: cross the sill, drop ~0.7 m into a trench, then face a 0.78 m vertical step up onto the dock. That is round 1's "the drive surface ended at the dock edge and resumed 0.7 m away" defect, now on the other side of the joint. The pack's one-way-floor gate cannot see it: test_fixed_surfaces_are_not_one_way_floors skips any triangle that is not entirely fixed nodes, and the tongue is all free.
findings.fix: Give the tongue a real landing. Cleanest fit to the fiction: add breakable landing beams from tongue_r2_c* down to dock_l_0/dock_r_0 in the same breakGroup as the straps, so the gangway is a genuine bridge until the release beat and swings away with the tire after it -- then relax test_only_the_straps_join_the_tire_to_the_dock from "exactly 2 bridges" to "every bridge is in STRAP_BREAK_GROUP". Add a gate that settles the cage and asserts every tongue node stays above DOCK_LANDING_Z - 0.05 both unloaded and under CAR_MASS.

findings.title: refNodes basis is degenerate: left-ref parallel to back-ref, up-ref points along +X
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py L2175 `cage.set_ground_reference(..., left=dock[("deck_l", 3)], up=dock[("deck_l", 0)])`; validated only for `back` in proplib/blender_kit.py::set_refnodes_existing
findings.problem: Measured from the handoff in BeamNG vehicle space: ref = ground_reference (-18.6, 0, 0); back-ref = (0, +3.000, 0); left-ref = dock_l_3 - ref = (0, +4.600, 0) -- identical direction to back, zero X component; up-ref = dock_l_0 - ref = (+13.175, +4.600, +0.780) -- 94% +X, 5.6% +Z. The engine builds the vehicle's reported orientation from these three edges; left is linearly dependent on back, and "up" is essentially world +X. Every other prop in the pack is clean (left = (+X, 0, 0), up = (0, 0, +Z)) -- I checked all 22 handoffs and colossus_tire is the only one whose left has no X component. Consequence is a vehicle transform rolled ~87 deg from reality: the external camera (cameraExternal distance 46, offset z 3) orbits with a sideways up-vector, and getDirectionVectorUp is wrong for anything that consults it. The runtime dodges it correctly (nodeWorldPosition sums getPosition + getNodePosition, insideTire fits the live axle), which is why it has not shown up.
findings.fix: Author a proper datum triad: keep ref/back as they are, add a ground_left node at (x2 + 3.0, 0, 0) and a ground_up node at (x2, 0, 1.5), and pass those. Then add the missing assert in blender_kit.set_ground_reference and set_refnodes_existing: the three edge vectors from ref must be linearly independent and each dominant along its intended axis (back +Y, left +X, up +Z). Right now only `back` is checked.

findings.title: Tie-down straps are still in compression at spawn - webbing pushing 8-12 kN
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py STRAP_SPEC (L506); tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::test_only_the_straps_join_the_tire_to_the_dock (L475)
findings.problem: The round-1 work order says "softened so they are not in compression at spawn". They are. Settling the shipped cage, at the gate's own 6000 steps both straps are in compression: dock_l_0 -> max_r_j46 at -8.15 kN and dock_r_0 -> max_r_j02 at -11.84 kN; at convergence -7.78 and -4.85 kN. What changed is that 60 kN beamDeform is no longer exceeded, so they stop yielding -- the sign never changed. Two nylon straps are visibly propping an 18 t tire up, and cutting them releases ~12.6 kN of stored compression as a lurch. Nothing gates this: the strap test checks count, family, breakGroup and strength ordering, and never looks at the settled force. Secondary: at beamDeform 60 kN the pair begins yielding at about 116 kNm of rolling torque, essentially identical to the 112.4 kNm a car at the traction limit applies -- so a committed boarding car deforms the tie-downs before the release beat, which is not "several times" the margin the spec claims.
findings.fix: Either pre-tension the straps (author them shorter than the settled distance so they are in tension at equilibrium) or make them non-compressive so the physics matches the material. Then extend test_only_the_straps_join_the_tire_to_the_dock to run _relax and assert every strap force is >= 0, and raise beamDeform so the yield margin over 112.4 kNm is the multiple the docstring claims.

findings.title: Contact-patch gate stops before convergence and counts gangway nodes on the floor
findings.where: tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::_relax (L383, `steps=6000`) and ::test_the_tire_settles_onto_a_real_contact_patch (L435)
findings.problem: Two independent measurement faults in the gate the round-1 patch fix was signed off against. First, 6000 steps is not converged: I get 11 contact nodes / 8.25 x 3.67 m at 6000 (exactly the figures in the work order), 15 nodes / 8.27 x 3.67 at 15000, and stable only past 40000. The shipped numbers are a transient. Second, the contact set is `free[index[identifier]] and z < 0.015` over ALL free nodes, and the gangway is free -- so once the solve does converge, six tongue nodes lying on the terrain enter the contact set and the gate reports 21 nodes / 9.47 x 5.32 m for a tire whose real footprint is 15 nodes / 8.27 x 3.66 m. It passes either way today, but it would keep passing if the tire lifted off the ground entirely, as long as the gangway were on the floor. That is the failure mode the brief warned about: the fix was verified by the thing that measures.
findings.fix: Raise steps to at least 40000 (or iterate to a residual-velocity tolerance instead of a fixed count), and restrict the contact set to carcass nodes with the existing `carcass_nodes` helper -- it already excludes the tongue and is used by the inertia test two functions up. findings.title: Tongue is bolted to the tire through a hinge line with no moment arm
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py L2155-2160, the port_frame beams from tongue[(0,column)] to sill_r and lin_r
findings.problem: Separate from the landing problem: the tongue's root has no rotational restraint. All 12 anchor beams run from tongue_r0 (x=-4.118, z~0.94-1.20) to sill_r (x=-4.683, z=0.934) and lin_r (x=-4.118, z=0.934) -- every anchor point is at essentially the same height as the row it holds, so the connection has ~zero lever arm in z and behaves as a frictionless hinge about the sill line. The tongue itself is a single-layer planar 6x3 truss with no depth, so it has no bending stiffness of its own either. In the settle the root row drops 0.21-0.40 m under nothing but the tongue's own 900 kg, while the sill it hangs from drops only 0.05 m -- a step down at the doorway before you even reach the dock. Fixing the landing (finding 3) turns it into a simply-supported span and hides most of this, but the joint is still a hinge.
findings.fix: Give the joint depth: run a second row of port_frame beams from tongue_r0 and tongue_r1 up to upp_r_j46..02 (x=-4.952, z=1.41-1.84), which are already there and are ~0.5-0.9 m above the sill. That is a real moment connection at the sill and costs 10 beams. While there, consider a second tongue node row 0.25 m below the deck so the gangway is a box truss rather than a sheet.

findings.title: Integrability gate checks the two stability bounds separately, not the joint one
findings.where: tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::test_the_cage_is_integrable_at_2000hz (L262), the two `assert ... < 0.9` at the end
findings.problem: For symplectic Euler with explicit damping the stability region is not two independent limits. With a = (omega*dt)^2 and b = c_total*dt/m, the amplification matrix has trace 2-a-b and determinant 1-b, so the condition is 0 <= b <= 2 AND a <= 4 - 2b -- the damping term eats spring headroom. The gate's two separate < 0.9 tests would admit a = 0.81 with b = 0.9 (joint 2.61) and call it safe on both counts without ever forming the coupled bound. The shipped cage is fine -- worst node sill_r_j00 gives a = 0.582, b = 0.867, joint 2.32 against 4, and no node comes close -- so this is about the gate outliving the current numbers, not about the tire.
findings.fix: Replace the two asserts with the joint form: assert (omega*DT)**2 + 2.0*(damping[i]*DT/mass) < 3.2 per node, and report the worst node's a and b in the message. The docstring's "c * dt / m must also stay under 2" should become the coupled statement.

findings.title: 44 beams join two fixed nodes and are integrated every step for nothing
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/mod/vehicles/ericrolph_colossus_tire/ericrolph_colossus_tire.jbeam - the 35 `dock` and 9 `rigid` beams, emitted from create_colossus_tire.py's dock lattice and set_ground_reference support_nodes
findings.problem: Both endpoints of all 44 are fixed:true, so their force is computed 2000 times a second and discarded (fixed nodes have acceleration zeroed). At 15 MN/m these are also the stiffest beams in the file, so they are the ones a reader checking the integrator bound trips over first. Harmless numerically, but it means the dock is 44 beams of decoration - if the intent was that the dock be a real structure, it is not; if the intent was that it be scenery, the beams should go.
findings.fix: Either drop beams whose endpoints are both fixed in proplib/prop_builder.py at emit time (one filter, and add a pack gate asserting none survive), or make the dock deck free nodes on a fixed base so the beams do work. The first is almost certainly what is wanted here.

findings.title: This mod's gate file is still documented as the round-1 tire, 8400/80R580

verdict_reason: The `prop` stage is genuinely excellent and I proved it rather than trusting it: `build.py colossus_tire prop` reproduces `mod/` and `textures/` byte-for-byte (`diff -rq` clean, including runtime.lua, jbeam, materials and all 40 PNGs); the generator's build-time asserts prove the numbers spec.py argues from (OD/W 2.722, rim/W 1.122, net-to-gross 70.7%, k_gyr 12.65 m, spin-up 15.9 s, 18000.0 kg over 1074 free nodes, sagitta 30.2 mm) instead of asserting them in prose; the palette is fully consumed (13/13, no orphan material); the strap chain resolves end to end (spec `strap_break_group` -> exactly 2 jbeam beams carrying `colossus_tiedown` -> `beamstate.breakBreakGroup`) and the new pack gate really does check it; and after a shared `lua_kit.propFrame` rewrite every one of the 22 mods still has tree == zip == lock (I hashed all 49 colossus members and every member of every other mod). The one-cage rule is honoured honestly: 1090 nodes in ONE component at spawn, splitting to 1074+16 only when the two strap beams break. But two things stop this being work I would stop and stare at. First, round 1's headline finding recurred inside its own fix: `assert_face_orientation` skips any object whose name matches no `ORIENTATION_RULES` fragment, so 37,140 of 144,944 tire triangles plus all 664 dock triangles are never judged, and one of the skipped objects — the BUILD_CODE sidewall band, on BOTH sidewalls — ships with its crown wound into the rubber (100.0% of crown-plane area inward), in a band no verify view frames. Second, the Blender stage is not reproducible: four builds of unchanged source gave four different DAEs, and `.gitignore:35` handles that by excluding `mod/`, `textures/` and `dist/` from Git — so no giant_props mod's shipped bytes can be re-derived from a clean checkout, and this 39 MB zip lock is one-shot. Add stale user-facing docs (the pack README still advertises the arithmetically-wrong `8400/80R580` that round-1 item 4 replaced) and 8 dead constants, and the pipeline reads as very strong in the half that is checked and unguarded in the half that is not.
round1_fixes_verified: #1 winding assert + culled renders — PARTIAL. assert_face_orientation() exists and runs every build, and verify_render.py does force use_backface_culling on every material. I also proved the checked-in renders are CURRENT, not stale: a fresh `--only hero` render matches the committed hero.jpg to mean-abs 0.13 / 0.25% of pixels >4 (EEVEE sampling noise). But measured coverage is 107,140 of 144,944 visual triangles; 29 of 40 tire objects and the entire dock are silently skipped, and one skipped band ships inverted.

#2 entry corridor — LANDED. Dock deck is 6/6 collision triangles up-facing (121.46 m2 up, 0 down); the gangway cage is real (18 free `tongue_*` nodes in a 3x6 grid, 20 collision triangles, 8.58 m2, 20/20 up-facing); the SILL meridian station measures r = 13.1504 m against CAVITY_RADIUS 13.1504 m exactly.
#3 contact patch — gate present and passing (test_the_tire_settles_onto_a_real_contact_patch, a 6000-step unilateral-contact relaxation), alongside the per-node Gershgorin bound at 2000 Hz.

#4 size code — LANDED IN CODE, NOT IN DOCS. spec.SIZE_CODE is 10350/80R457 and assert_authored_claims() rejects OD/W and rim/W outside EARTHMOVER_OD_TO_WIDTH / EARTHMOVER_RIM_TO_WIDTH at build time (printed 2.722 / 1.122). Four docstrings and the pack README still say 8400/80R580.

#5 sRGB — LANDED and safe. Tread colour byte mean measured 57.89 (matches the claim); _srgb_encode is opt-in per palette entry with `srgb=False` default in prop_builder.ensure_textures, so the other 20 mods' tuned output is untouched. Roughness/normal maps correctly stay linear.
#6 tread net-to-gross — LANDED. assert_authored_claims computes it off TREAD_ROWS/TREAD_PITCHES/LATERAL_GROOVE and gates it against NET_TO_GROSS_BAND; generator prints 70.7%.

#7 lettering stacked and centred — the stack/fit asserts are real (SystemExit if the stack overshoots the mouldable band, plus a per-band re-check), but the geometry produced for the lowest band is inside out on both sidewalls; see finding 1.

#11 TIRE_MASS from one torque — LANDED. Generator prints and gates 'free (tire) mass: 18000.0 kg over 1074 free nodes', with RADIUS_OF_GYRATION and SPINUP_SECONDS_BAND both asserted (12.65 m, 15.9 s).

#16/#21 degenerate triangles and gates — LANDED. Generator prints 'degenerate dropped: 0'; 13 geometry gates + 17 pack gates = the claimed 30, all passing. The three new pack gates resolve real chains: I traced test_behaviour_node_names_resolve_in_the_jbeam's regex onto the actual `strap_break_group = "colossus_tiedown"` literal at runtime.lua:78 and confirmed it matches the 2 beams that carry it.

findings.title: Winding assert skips 26% of the mesh; one skipped band ships inside out
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/blender/create_colossus_tire.py — ORIENTATION_RULES / assert_face_orientation() (`if rule is None: continue`), and build_lettering()
findings.problem: The docstring says "Every visual face must point OUT of the rubber", but the function matches object names against a fragment table and `continue`s on a miss. Measured on the current tree by exec'ing the generator with main() stripped and calling the builders: 107,140 of 144,944 visual triangles carry a rule; 37,140 tire triangles across 29 of 40 objects match nothing (all 20 `letter_*`, `port_bezel`, `port_cut`, `tongue`, `tongue_kerb`, `tongue_ribs`, the straps), and all 664 dock triangles are never passed to the function at all — main() calls it on `tire_objects` only. That hole is not theoretical: `letter_9` and `letter_19` (the BUILD_CODE band, one per sidewall) have 100.0% of their crown-plane area facing inboard, n.x = +0.902 on the -X sidewall and -0.902 on the +X sidewall, opposite in sign to all 18 sibling glyphs, and signed volume -0.45 against +1.4..+9.6 for the siblings. build_lettering's `bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals` fails on that band — plausibly because the `stand = ... + max(local.z, 0.0) * 2.0` bend flattens the back half of the extrusion, leaving the strongest-bent (smallest-radius) band without a well-defined inside. BeamNG backface-culls flexbodies, so that moulded band is see-through in game. Nothing caught it because no verify view frames it either: the band sits at radius ~6.58 m (one copy per side at theta = TAU*0.5) while `sidewall_print` in verify_render.py:VIEWS looks at radius ~8.6 m, where SIZE_CODE lives. This is round-1 finding #1's exact failure mode, recurring inside its own fix.
findings.fix: Make the gate fail closed: in assert_face_orientation, collect objects whose name matches no fragment and raise SystemExit listing them, so new geometry cannot enter the mesh unjudged. Add rules for `letter` (`away_from_centre_plane`), `port_bezel`/`port_cut`/`tongue*` and `strap`, and pass dock_objects through it too with an `up`/`away_from_shell` rule. Then fix the winding itself — after the recalc in build_lettering, measure the max-|x| polygon's normal against the sidewall's outboard direction and flip_normals() if it disagrees, which is deterministic where recalc's inside/outside heuristic is not. Finally add a verify view framing the BUILD_CODE band radius (~6.6 m) so the review set covers every band the generator emits.

findings.title: Blender stage not reproducible: four builds of one source, four different DAEs
findings.where: examples/giant_props/proplib/blender_kit.py — _export_selected_collada() / export_multi_flexbody(); .gitignore:35
findings.problem: I ran `blender --factory-startup --background --python create_colossus_tire.py` twice with no source change and got DAEs of 25,343,535 and 25,343,619 bytes against the shipped 25,343,770 — three distinct sha256s, plus a fourth (839653dc…) from the concurrent session's own rebuild. The handoff diff isolates it exactly: of 16 top-level keys only `visual` changes — nodes, beams, triangles, beam_specs, refnodes and behavior are bit-stable. Root causes located: (a) the DAE header carries `<created>2026-08-25T00:36:53</created>` and `<modified>` wall-clock stamps; (b) UV float jitter — comparing `<float_array>` blocks between runs, only the `map-0-array` sources differ (82 of 1,076,400 carcass values at max delta 1e-7, 234 of 23,568 dock values at 1e-6) while position and normal arrays are byte-identical, i.e. last-ULP noise out of modifier evaluation. This is pack-wide, not colossus-specific: rebuilding hot_potato changed both of its DAEs too. .gitignore:35 already documents the behaviour and responds by excluding `examples/giant_props/*/mod/`, `textures/` and `dist/` from Git — so the tracked `authoring/*.handoff.json` pins a sha256 of an untracked file that no rebuild can reproduce, a clean clone cannot re-derive any mod's shipped bytes, and colossus's 39,120,034-byte / df271d2b… zip lock is a one-shot artifact. AGENTS.md's own rule — compare each mod/ worktree byte hash with its Git blob before locking a release — is unrunnable for this pack.
findings.fix: _export_selected_collada already post-processes the file via _strip_absolute_image_paths, so extend that hook: rewrite `<created>`/`<modified>` to a fixed epoch (the same per-release constant pattern build_distribution.py uses) and `<author>Blender User</author>` to the pack author. In export_multi_flexbody, quantize each merged mesh's active UV layer (round to 1e-6) after `bpy.ops.object.transform_apply` and before _export_selected_collada, which removes the ULP class entirely. Then add a pack gate that runs one generator twice into a tmp dir and asserts identical DAE bytes, and un-ignore `mod/` so the shipped tree is reviewable and the Git-blob comparison AGENTS.md mandates becomes possible.

findings.title: Neither new winding gate can see the surfaces the car is actually driven on
findings.where: tests/test_giant_props_pack.py::test_fixed_surfaces_are_not_one_way_floors; tests/test_colossus_tire_geometry.py::test_collision_triangles_face_the_right_way
findings.problem: The pack gate skips any triangle that is not all-fixed (`if not all(fixed.get(i) for i in identifiers): continue`). Colossus's boarding gangway is 18 FREE `tongue_*` nodes carrying 20 collision triangles over 8.58 m2 — the surface a car drives on to board — so the gate is structurally blind to it, as it is to the entire cavity floor. The mod-local gate covers only the crown and liner bands: I counted 768 of 3,226 collision triangles judged, leaving the sill/shoulder/upper/lower/bead bands (2,458 triangles) and the gangway with zero winding coverage from anything. The aggregate form is also weak where it does apply: colossus's fixed horizontal set is 121.46 m2 up / 0.00 m2 down over 6 triangles, so 63.9 m2 — half the loading dock — could invert and the `up >= 0.9 * down` test would still pass. Both surfaces happen to be correct today (I measured gangway 20/20 up-facing, dock 6/6 up-facing), so this is a gate gap rather than a live defect — but it is the same gap that let round-1's six down-facing deck triangles ship.
findings.fix: Change test_fixed_surfaces_are_not_one_way_floors to group triangles by the handoff's node `group` field instead of requiring all-fixed, and assert the up/down ratio PER GROUP — a per-surface test catches a half-inverted deck that the aggregate cannot, and it starts covering free-node decks. In test_collision_triangles_face_the_right_way, extend `band_of` past crown/liner: add `sill_*`/`shl_*`/`upp_*`/`low_*`/`bead_*` with the radial rule they already satisfy, and add an explicit `tongue_*` case asserting the deck faces up, then raise the `checked` floors so a band silently dropping out of the table fails the gate.

findings.title: Eight dead constants in spec.py, several of them numbers the design argues from
findings.where: examples/giant_props/colossus_tire/spec.py — CAVITY_LANE:409, SPINUP_TARGET_SECONDS:456, PORT_LIFT_LUGS:546, DOCK_GRADE:599, SPEW_PER_STATION:735, CROWN_DROP:298, CAR_WIDTH:247, CAR_TURN_RADIUS:251; examples/giant_props/proplib/prop_builder.py::ensure_textures
findings.problem: I AST-scanned all 157 upper-case module constants and cross-referenced the generator, verify_render, both gate files, prop_builder and lua_kit (accounting for the dynamic `getattr(spec, name)` path BAND_SCALES uses): eight are read by nothing. They are not inert trivia — PORT_LIFT_LUGS = 4 sits beside a call site that hardcodes strap_lug_points() + 2 literal corner lugs; SPINUP_TARGET_SECONDS = 15.0 duplicates the SPINUP_SECONDS_BAND that assert_authored_claims actually gates on; CAR_TURN_RADIUS = 5.2 sits beside test_cavity_clears_a_car's magic `CAR_LENGTH + 2.0`; SPEW_PER_STATION = 5 ("moulded vent whiskers") drives no geometry. findings.problem: Every giant_props DAE ships Blender's default `<author>Blender User</author>` and a full `<authoring_tool>` string naming the local build hash. AGENTS.md's namespacing section wants Repository-facing assets stamped with the author-plus-mod identity, and the pack is otherwise scrupulous about it (mod id, jbeam part keys, material names, mapTo, Lua extension name, trigger names all carry `ericrolph_`). This is the one place the machine's identity rather than the author's leaks into a public artifact.
findings.fix: Set the author string in the same post-export pass as the `<created>`/`<modified>` fix from finding 2 — one regex substitution in _strip_absolute_image_paths covers all 22 mods at once, and folding it into that change means it costs no extra rebuild.
